text:
Situation: Remifentanil hydrochloride 2 mg/2 mL, 5 mL vials are short at Corvale Lakeside (15 vials, 6.8 days) while Corvale General holds 130 vials (16.5 days). A rule‑based transfer of 16 vials from General to Lakeside would give Lakeside 14 days on hand and leave General with two weeks.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the remifentanil hydrochloride shortage on 2022‑06‑28 and it remains current as of 2026‑10‑21. The listing includes Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc., and Mylan Institutional, a Viatris Company. Our sites use Hikma‑labeled product NDC 00143939210, linked to Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) and Navinta LLC (FEI 3004375014). FDA inspection 1064827 at Hospira ended 2018‑08‑15, classified OAI with letter dated 2020‑04‑22 (797 days before shortage posting). FDA inspection 971010 at Navinta ended 2016‑05‑16, classified OAI with letter dated 2018‑04‑20 (1,530 days before shortage posting).

Our position: Transfer is the fastest way to protect Lakeside supply without new procurement. Both sites use the same NDC.

Recommended actions:
1. Pharmacy Director approves the inter‑site transfer of 16 vials from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside.
2. Controlled Substance Coordinator executes a DEA Form 222 or CSOS order for the Schedule II transfer.
3. Buyer confirms receipt and updates inventory records at both sites.

Not recommended: Purchasing alternative manufacturers or concentrations at this time; the transfer resolves the immediate gap and the shortage remains active per FDA.
